Bratslav Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Vinnytska oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Bratslav was home to Rabbi Nahman of Bratslav, founder of Breslov Hasidism, who lived in the town from 1810; his disciple Natan Steinherz (likely Nathan Sternhartz, Rebbe Nachman's chief scribe) established a Hebrew press here in 1819 to publish his teachings, and Sternhartz's own son later led a Bratslav Hasidic community in nearby Tulchyn, documented elsewhere in this collection. The town endured 14 separate pogroms between May 1919 and March 1921 alone, killing over 200 people, and during WWII, 1,840 Jews were executed — very nearly the community's entire prewar population. Only around 50 Jews remained by 2014, the same year the community regained permission to use the town's large synagogue; today Bratslav is a major site of Hasidic pilgrimage, drawing an estimated 7,000 Breslover Hasidic visitors annually. The opera singer Rosalia Gorskaya was born here in 1891.
